dataset.description: The dataset contains goat milk composition (fat, protein, lactose, urea content, dry matter, freezing point, somatic cell count, casein content etc), goat milk coagulation properties, as curd firmness. This parameters describes goat milk quality and it variations in different seasons, lactation stage, animal breed, diet etc.

distribution.title: The data is collected to understand goat milk quality parameters and it's connection to cheese production, to get better cheese outcome.

dataset.title: Goat milk quality

dmp.description:
The composition of milk and the relationship between its composition (fat and protein; fat and casein; casein fraction: α, β and κ) are crucial for cheese production. Parameters determine milk coagulation time and the density of the resulting curd, the yield of the cheese, the loss of fat and protein with whey. In Latvia, raw cheeses are mainly made from goat's milk, besides producers do not pay attention to the consumption of raw materials for obtaining one unit of production. With the development of commercial goat milk processing, these issues are crucial for long-term farming and for the production of products of constant quality, especially matured fresh milk cheeses. This is why the industrial cheese producers develop slowly, because it is difficult to ensure the independent quality of the raw material for the production of certain dairy products. The planned study and its insights can help goat milk processors understand the relationship between the changes in milk composition and their usability in the production of certain cheeses, including the importance of the number of somatic cells in the yield of the cheese and the production of technological losses.

Most studies in Latvia have focused on the importance on goat welfare, hygiene and genetics for increasing milk yield in dairy production. Animal nutrition and genetics can change the composition of milk, but any change must also be assessed from the point of view of the suitability of the milk in the production of milk products, especially cheese.

The aim of the study is to analyze the quality of goat milk suitability for cheese production in Latvia.

Study tasks:

1. To examine the composition of goat milk obtained in Latvia, the relationship between individual ingredients for ensuring the necessary technological characteristics for cheese production;

2. To analyze seasonal effects on the composition, quality and sensory characteristics of goat milk;

3. Analyze the number of somatic cell count in goat milk, the relationship between their changes in season and lactation number and stage;

4. To assess the coagulation characteristics of the goat milk and the factors influencing it for the cheese production;

5. Assess the suitability of goat milk for the production of soft and semi-hard fresh milk cheeses, optimization of their quality and yield.

The results of the study would help leading goat milk producing companies develop production of economically justified products, large Latvian processing enterprises overcome diminished stereotypes for processing goat's milk and production of products, would be a solution for rational use of rapidly growing goat's milk in food and products important for public health.
